messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PD Alert - prom-scrape-job DOWN for job=redwood-exporters (3 targets failing) - paging eng-sre_oncall
Alex K: acked on PD, digging in. seeing spikes in scrape errors, looks like 503s from the scrape-proxy.
Morgan: thanks - are logs backing up? any sign of prom-push or logbuffer pressure?
Sam L: log ingestion queue depth jumped ~40k in last 2m, saw a bunch of 429s from logstore in the tails of the pipeline. linking logs: https://ops.redwood/logs?q=job:prom-scrape+error
Alex K: running quick check of scrape targets

Alex K: ```curl -s "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/targets?state=down" | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | {scrapePool, lastError, scrapeUrl}'```
Alex K: results: exporter-hosts returning 503 on /metrics, lastError shows "EOF" then "connection reset" across 3 hosts.
Taylor (oncall): i'm taking primary. handoff from Alex - please add me to PD if not already.
Alex K: added @Taylor, @Morgan. PD note: root cause likely scrape-proxy -> backend LB returning 503s. I'll try restart of proxy pod.
Morgan: customer impact check: internal dashboards show missing http_request_rate for a few customers in EU region since ~10:15UTC. pausing canary dashboards.
Lee: observed log forwarder (promtail) connection errors: TLS handshake timeouts to logstore, possibly saturating egress. That could explain 429s upstream.
Taylor (oncall): coordinated plan: 1) isolate scrape-proxy error by restarting pods; 2) if 503 persists, failover LB to secondary; 3) backfill missing metrics once scrape resumes; 4) escalate to infra if network egress saturated.
Sam L: restarting scrape-proxy pod now (k8s): ```kubectl -n infra delete pod scrape-proxy-5d7f8``` will let deployment recreate.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Pod scrape-proxy-5d7f8 deleted - new pod scrape-proxy-9c4b2 scheduling
Alex K: monitoring prom target status... new pod came up, but still seeing 503s from different IPs.
Morgan: seems like the LB upstream is returning 503 intermittently. checking AWS NLB metrics.
Lee: NLB 5xx rate spiked at the same time as egress TLS errors. i'm suspecting an MTU/path issue or recent network config change.
Taylor (oncall): good catch. can infra check network ACLs / sg changes in last 30m? @ops-infra
Alex K: meanwhile, to reduce customer impact, enable fallback routing for scrape requests to secondary-exporter pool. adding temporary routing rule in envoy: ```envoy route add /metrics -> pool-b```
Sam L: added route change, confirming: curl to exporter hits pool-b and returns 200 now for one host.
Morgan: customer dashboards are starting to show metrics backfill for some tenants. great.
Taylor (oncall): PD escalation level remains at P1 until all exporters stable and log queues drain below 5k.
Alex K: running backlog drain script for logs: ```python tools/drain_backlog.py --target 5000 --dry-run``` going to run real now.
Sam L: running backlog drain. ETA ~ 15m for 40k -> 5k with current throughput.
Lee: infra update in PD thread: "No recent SG changes. Found increased packet drops on egress path to logstore endpoint - engaged cloud network team." quoted.
Taylor (oncall): thanks infra. is there any customer-facing action? Do we need to notify support/ops?
Morgan: opened a short status note for support: "Investigating missing metrics and delayed logs for EU customers. Engineers are mitigating; minimal data gaps expected for ~30-45m." posted to #customer-ops and status page.
Alex K: prom targets now stable (3/3 UP) but scrape latency higher. continuing to watch for 10m.
Sam L: backlog at 18k and dropping. 429s are almost gone.
Taylor (oncall): handoff plan: i'll stay on for the next 30m; if backlog < 5k and prom targets stable for 15m, we'll close the PD and follow up with a postmortem.
Lee: adding follow-ups: check tcp_mss/MTU on hosts, verify envoy/mTLS handshake timers, and add circuit-breaker for scrape-proxy to avoid thundering restarts.
incident-bot: PD update: incident resolved - page closed by Taylor (oncall).
Taylor (oncall): closing thread summary: root cause likely transient egress network degradation causing TLS handshake failures to logstore -> upstream 429/503 cascade. Mitigation: restarted scrape-proxy, failover routing to pool-b, backlog drain, infra engaged. Customer impact: missing metrics and delayed logs for EU customers between 10:14-10:38 UTC; no data loss after backfill. Follow-up: infra to provide network postmortem, eng-sre to draft RCA and add circuit breaker on scrape-proxy. Assignments: Lee (network debug + MTU), Sam L (backfill verification), Alex K (envoy circuit-breaker PR), Morgan (RCA doc). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
